Q: Firebase auth/invalid-credential "Invalid OAuth response from apple.com" with valid identityToken A:

A valid Apple identityToken does not necessarily mean Firebase will accept the credential created by:

OAuthProvider('apple.com').credential(
  idToken: appleCredential.identityToken,
  rawNonce: rawNonce,
)

There is a known FlutterFire/iOS issue around this path.

The generic OAuthProvider('apple.com') credential can end up sending an empty access_token parameter to Firebase:

providerId=apple.com&id_token=<token>&nonce=<nonce>&access_token=

Firebase then treats the request differently and returns:

INVALID_IDP_RESPONSE: Invalid OAuth response from apple.com

even though the id_token itself is valid.

That matches the symptoms in the question: valid iss, aud, expiry and nonce, but AuthenticationService.SignInWithIdp still rejects the credential.

For native Apple sign-in, use the Apple-specific credential API instead of the generic OAuthProvider API:

final appleCredential =
    await SignInWithApple.getAppleIDCredential(
  scopes: [
    AppleIDAuthorizationScopes.email,
    AppleIDAuthorizationScopes.fullName,
  ],
  nonce: sha256.convert(utf8.encode(rawNonce)).toString(),
);

final idToken = appleCredential.identityToken;
if (idToken == null) {
  throw StateError('Apple did not return an identity token');
}

final credential = AppleAuthProvider.credentialWithIDToken(
  idToken,
  rawNonce,
  AppleFullPersonName(
    givenName: appleCredential.givenName,
    familyName: appleCredential.familyName,
  ),
);

await FirebaseAuth.instance.signInWithCredential(credential);

FlutterFire's own documentation shows this Apple-specific API for the native iOS flow:

AppleAuthProvider.credentialWithIDToken(
  idToken,
  rawNonce,
  fullName,
);

rather than constructing the credential with:

OAuthProvider('apple.com').credential(...)

There have also been multiple FlutterFire reports of Invalid OAuth response from apple.com with a valid Apple JWT when using the generic credential path.

So I would try changing the credential construction before changing the Apple Developer or Firebase Console configuration again.

The Services ID / .p8 OAuth configuration is primarily relevant to flows where Firebase performs the Apple OAuth exchange. For a native iOS flow where Apple has already returned the ID token, repeatedly recreating those settings will not fix a client-side credential-construction bug.

Also, do not pass the Apple authorizationCode as accessToken merely to make this error disappear. That has been reported as a workaround, but the Apple-specific credential API is the cleaner solution.

The Russian phone-number problem is unrelated and should really be a separate Stack Overflow question. Combining it with the Apple authentication issue makes both problems harder to diagnose.

References:

  • FlutterFire federated authentication - Apple
  • Firebase: Authenticate Using Apple on iOS
  • FlutterFire issue #18445 - empty access_token causing Invalid OAuth response from apple.com
  • FlutterFire issue #18289 - valid Apple token rejected with invalid-credential
  • FlutterFire issue #18325 - native Apple sign-in rejected despite valid JWT

Q: Fixed point vs Floating point number A:

Real-world example: Money is commonly represented using fixed decimal places, while scientific calculations commonly use floating-point numbers.

Fixed-point number:

A fixed-point number stores the decimal point at a fixed position.

Example:
If we decide to keep 2 digits after the decimal:

10.25
25.50
100.75

The decimal point always stays after 2 digits.

Floating-point number:
A floating-point number allows the decimal point to move depending on the size of the number.

Example:

12345.67 can be represented as 1.234567 × 10⁴

0.001234 can be represented as 1.234 × 10⁻³

So, in simple terms:

Fixed-point = decimal point stays fixed.
Floating-point = decimal point can move.

Q: How to run an async function weekly at a specific time A:

There are a couple of separate problems here.

The first one is in delay_until():

if (
    day.capitalize() not in days
    or day.capitalize() != "Tomorrow"
    or hour < 0
    or hour > 24
):

For "Sunday", day.capitalize() != "Tomorrow" is True, so this condition always returns:

"Invalid date provided"

You then effectively do:

await asyncio.sleep("Invalid date provided")

instead of passing a number of seconds.

The validation should test whether the value is neither a weekday nor "Tomorrow":

if (
    day.capitalize() not in days
    and day.capitalize() != "Tomorrow"
) or not 0 <= hour <= 23:
    raise ValueError("Invalid date provided")

Note that 24 is not a valid datetime hour; the valid range is 0 through 23.

There is another issue here:

function=demo_fx(),

This calls demo_fx immediately and passes its return value (None) to schedule.

Pass the function itself instead:

function=demo_fx

Also, asyncio.gather() expects awaitable objects. Your demo_fx() is a normal synchronous function, so it cannot be passed directly to gather().

If the function you are scheduling can be asynchronous, make it a coroutine:

async def demo_fx():
    print("hello world")

and simplify the scheduler to:

async def schedule(delay, loop_time, function, *args, **kwargs):
    await asyncio.sleep(delay)

    while True:
        await function(*args, **kwargs)
        await asyncio.sleep(loop_time)

There is one more edge case in delay_until(): if today is already the requested weekday and the requested time has passed, the modulo calculation selects today and produces a negative delay.

It is simpler to construct the target datetime and move it forward a week when necessary:

from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone
import asyncio

days = {
    "Monday": 0,
    "Tuesday": 1,
    "Wednesday": 2,
    "Thursday": 3,
    "Friday": 4,
    "Saturday": 5,
    "Sunday": 6,
}

def delay_until(day: str, hour: int) -> float:
    day = day.capitalize()

    if day not in days or not 0 <= hour <= 23:
        raise ValueError("Invalid date provided")

    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc)

    target = now.replace(
        hour=hour,
        minute=0,
        second=0,
        microsecond=0,
    )

    target += timedelta(
        days=(days[day] - now.weekday()) % 7
    )

    if target <= now:
        target += timedelta(weeks=1)

    return (target - now).total_seconds()


async def schedule(delay, interval, function, *args, **kwargs):
    await asyncio.sleep(delay)

    while True:
        await function(*args, **kwargs)
        await asyncio.sleep(interval)


async def demo_fx():
    print("hello world")


async def main():
    await schedule(
        delay_until("Sunday", 19),
        timedelta(weeks=1).total_seconds(),
        demo_fx,
    )


asyncio.run(main())

asyncio.sleep() suspends the current task, so while it is waiting it does not block the event loop from running the other tasks in the bot.

One distinction is worth mentioning: this sleeps for one week after each execution. If you specifically need "Sunday at 19:00 UTC" every time, rather than "604800 seconds after the previous execution", calculate the next target again on every iteration. That also becomes important when scheduling in a local timezone that observes daylight-saving changes.

Documentation:

  • asyncio.sleep()
  • asyncio.gather()
  • Coroutines and awaitables
  • datetime.weekday()
  • datetime.timedelta
  • asyncio.run()

Q: ORA-12514 TNS:listener does not currently know of service requested in connect descriptor in oracle 11g A:

I have this problem in windows 10 and Oracle19C. You should try the following ways and one of them may work for you.

Way-1: In windows: use this video: restart services OracleOraDB19Home1TNSListener then OracleServiceORCL.

Way-2: connect with system user password to sql plus as shown as:

Enter user-name: system/ as sysdba
Enter password: your_password

SQL> shutdown
SQL> startup nomount
SQL> alter system set db_recovery_file_dest_size=4G scope=both;
SQL> alter database mount;
SQL> alter database open;

And now check your problem fixed? If no set below code then check again.

SQL> alter system set local_listener='(DESCRIPTION=(ADDRESS=(PROTOCOL=tcp)   (HOST=127.0.0.1) (PORT=1521)))';

This work for me.
